originalTitle: US stocks today: Nasdaq ends lower as chip weakness offsets solid earnings, economic data
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the US stock market: the Nasdaq, which is a group of stocks, ended the day with a lower value. This happened because companies that make computer chips, like semiconductors, didn't do well, which pulled the whole market down. Even though some other areas, like healthcare, did well, and economic data looked good, the chip companies' weakness had a bigger impact. This is causing investors to be careful and uncertain about what will happen next, even though some positive signs, like strong retail sales, suggest the economy is still doing okay. Overall, the market is being volatile, or changing quickly, which is making investors cautious.

originalTitle: Fed's Logan calls for 'modestly higher' interest rates
simplifiedContent: A top official at the Federal Reserve, Lorie Logan, thinks that interest rates should be slightly higher. This is because she believes that inflation (or the rate at which prices are rising) is still too high, and the current interest rates are not doing enough to slow it down. Logan also mentioned that there are potential risks to the economy, including strong demand for goods and services, investments in artificial intelligence, and tensions in the Middle East. This matters because the Federal Reserve is set to meet in July to decide on interest rates, and Logan's comments suggest that there may be different opinions among the decision-makers. This could impact the direction of interest rates and the overall economy.

originalTitle: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | S&P 500 | US Stock Market Today | Highlights: Nasdaq ends lower as chip weakness offsets solid earnings, economic data
simplifiedContent: The US stock market had a mixed day, with the Nasdaq ending lower. This happened because companies that make computer chips had a bad day, which offset good news from other companies that released strong earnings. Some positive economic data was also released, but it wasn't enough to lift the Nasdaq. The Dow Jones and S&P 500 are other important stock market measures, but the article doesn't say how they did. The Nasdaq's decline matters because it shows that even when some companies do well, weaknesses in other areas can still bring down the overall market.

originalTitle: Netflix earnings in focus as shares gain slightly amid growth concerns
simplifiedContent: Here is a simplified version of the news item: Netflix is about to release its quarterly earnings report, which is a document that shows how well the company did financially. Wall Street, which is like a group of investors and experts, thinks Netflix will say it made around $13 billion in the last quarter, which is 14% more than it made the same time last year. They also think the company will report that it made 79 cents per share, which is 10% more than last year. This matters because it will affect the price of Netflix shares, which have gone up a little bit lately despite some concerns about the company's growth. Overall, investors are watching closely to see if Netflix meets these expectations.

originalTitle: Gold, silver prices today: Comex gold and silver extend losses as Middle East tensions fuel rate hike fears
simplifiedContent: The prices of gold and silver have gone down again. This is because of increasing tensions in the Middle East, which is making people think that the US will raise interest rates. When interest rates go up, it can make gold and silver less attractive to investors, so people are selling them, which drives their prices down. As a result, gold fell to $3,977 and silver fell to $55.65. This matters because it affects the value of investments in these precious metals.

originalTitle: Caliber Mining IPO raises  ₹135 crore from anchor investors ahead of issue opening
simplifiedContent: Caliber Mining and Logistics Limited is getting ready to sell its shares to the public through an Initial Public Offering (IPO) that starts on July 17, 2026. Before the IPO, the company has already raised ₹134.99 crore from important investors, known as anchor investors. These investors bought 31,83,961 shares at a price of ₹424 each. This is significant because it shows that these big investors are interested in the company, which might attract more investors when the IPO opens. The money raised will go to the company, and this development can indicate a positive start to its IPO.
